intro:
Lymphatic circulation care

LYMPHATIC CARE PROGRAMME — swelling relief · circulation care · condition care during recovery

Often called "lymphatic detox", this care gently supports the flow of lymph — the body's fluid channels. At Myeongdong Mirae Cell Clinic the doctor sees you first, and the order and pressure of the session are then set to suit you.

What makes us different?

The doctor examines you before any care

Swelling can be simple fatigue, but it can also signal a clot or a heart or kidney problem. In those cases lymphatic care can be harmful. Here the doctor consults with you first and checks whether the care is safe for you at all.

Regeneration is cells; circulation is lymph

This clinic has practised anti-ageing care centred on stem cells. Restoring cells (regeneration) and keeping the body's fluid channels moving (circulation) are two different things, and both are needed. Lymphatic care covers the second.

From the surgery through to recovery

Swelling follows procedures such as liposuction or fat grafting. Manually opening the lymphatic pathways is used as a supportive method for managing post-operative swelling. The team that knows your surgical course continues the care.

This may suit you if

  • your face swells in the morning, or your legs in the evening
  • you sit or stand all day at work
  • you hold one posture for long periods and feel heavy and tired
  • you have entered the recovery phase after surgery and your medical team has cleared you
  • you have been diagnosed with lymphoedema and need ongoing care

※ The reason for swelling differs from person to person. We check first, at the consultation, whether this care is suitable for you.

How is it different from a massage?

This is not deep kneading.

Lymphatic vessels run just beneath the skin. Pressing hard and deep therefore blocks the flow rather than helping it. This care uses very light pressure, sweeping along the direction of flow as water would run.

What matters instead is the order. The places where lymph gathers — neck, armpits, groin — are opened first, and only then is fluid moved from the swollen area towards them. The path is cleared before the water is sent.

What happens on the day?

  1. Consultation with the doctorWhen the swelling began and how it behaves, any surgery or treatment you have had, any conditions you live with. This is where we decide whether the care is appropriate for you.
  2. Condition checkWe look at the skin and each area. If there is redness, heat or a wound, the session is postponed that day.
  3. The sessionWe begin with shoulder rotation and abdominal breathing to open the central pathways first. Then we work from the healthy side's lymph nodes towards the swollen area.
  4. Guidance for homeWe show you how to continue at home — compression, movement and skin care.

What is lymph?

If blood vessels are the motorway, lymphatic vessels are the waterway alongside it.

Fluid is constantly moving between the cells of the body. The lymphatic vessels collect that fluid and carry it back towards the heart. Valves inside them stop the fluid running backwards, so lymph always flows in one direction — towards the heart.

Lymph does three things.

  • It carries — moving fluid around the body
  • It clears — filtering damaged cells out of the body
  • It defends — producing and managing the white blood cells that fight infection

Sitting for long periods, having surgery, or holding a lopsided posture all slow this flow. Fluid then pools, and is felt as swelling, heaviness and tightness.
outro:
When this care cannot be given

This care does not diagnose or treat any disease

Lymphatic care speeds up flow inside the body. It can therefore dislodge a clot or spread inflammation. If any of the following applies to you, this care cannot be given, or you must speak to a doctor first.

  • a clot in a blood vessel (thrombosis, deep vein thrombosis)
  • spreading inflammation under the skin, or a fever (cellulitis and similar)
  • heart or kidney disease, or a history of stroke (heart failure, renal failure, stroke)
  • undergoing cancer treatment, or cancer tissue in the area to be treated
  • recent surgery — we begin only after your medical team judges you to be in recovery
  • skin that is red, hot or broken — stop and seek medical care

Frequently asked questions

Will one session make a difference?
Not dramatically. It varies from person to person, and it is more usual to combine the care with compression management.
Will I lose weight?
No. Losing swelling and losing weight are different things. There is no evidence that lymphatic care reduces body weight.
Does it remove toxins from the body?
No reliable evidence of a "detox" effect in healthy people has been established. The purpose of this care is relief of swelling and management of flow.
Does it hurt or leave bruises?
It is done with very light pressure, so it is unlike a deep-pressure massage.
How soon after surgery can I have it?
It is not advised immediately after surgery. We set the starting point at a consultation, once your medical team judges you to be in recovery.

Please note

  • This care is carried out after consultation and according to your individual condition. It does not diagnose or treat disease.
  • Results and satisfaction vary with individual condition and daily habits.
  • If swelling persists, affects one side only, or comes with pain or heat, medical examination comes before care.
